judged_text: The duplicate-guest and blacklist filters compare emails case-sensitively: guest === attendee.email, and blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) tests an un-lowercased guest against a lowercased list. Submitting 'John@Example.com' when 'john@example.com' already attends bypasses the dedup and creates a second attendee row for the same person (who then receives both a guests-added email and a duplicate scheduled email), and any uppercase variant of a BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entry bypasses the blacklist entirely.

record.issue_text: [BUG] The duplicate-guest and blacklist filters compare emails case-sensitively: guest === attendee.email, and blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) tests an un-lowercased guest against a lowercased list. Submitting 'John@Example.com' when 'john@example.com' already attends bypasses the dedup and creates a second attendee row for the same person (who then receives both a guests-added email and a duplicate scheduled email), and any uppercase variant of a BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entry bypasses the blacklist entirely.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with case-sensitive comparisons: it filters out existing attendees via `guest === attendee.email` and filters blacklisted emails via `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. However, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is explicitly lowercased (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) while `guest` is not, so case variants bypass the blacklist. Likewise, case variants of an existing attendee email are not deduped and will be inserted via `attendees.createMany`, creating duplicate attendee rows for the same email differing only by case.
